newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai air force supports airport extension plan.
newsitem.headline: Thai air force supports airport extension plan.

text.p: The commander of the Royal Thai Air Force on Wednesday pledged full support for a government plan to extend Bangkok airport into land owned by the force.
The Thai government on Tuesday agreed to suspend a 100 billion baht ($4 billion) project to build a second airport at Nong Ngu Hao in Bangkok's eastern outskirts.
It decided instead to concentrate on expanding the existing Don Muang airport, built on land owned by the Royal Thai Air Force. Don Muang is adjacent to the Air Force headquarters.
Air Chief Marshal Amorn Naewmalee said the air force was ready to sacrifice its land.
"For the sake of the interest of the country the air force is ready give away part of the land for the expansion of the current airport," Amorn told reporters.
He said details of how the airport would be expanded must still be worked out.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchiayudh, who is also Defence Minister, said on Tuesday the air force had pledged to cooperate with the government and relocate air force installations.
Government officials said cabinet made the decision because it had to exercise strict monetary discipline.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told the Japanese ambassador on Wednesday that Thailand had not completely scrapped the idea of the second airport, but only put it on hold.
He told reporters after meeting the Japanese diplomat, Hiroshi Ota, that the government would expand Don Muang until the project was restarted. He did not give further details.
The airport can handle a maximum of 31 million passengers and 600,000 tonnes of cargo a year. Analysts say demand could rise to as many as 58 million passengers per year in the next decade.
The Nong Ngu Hao project was initiated in 1960 but due to indecision by different governments, little progress was made.
